projects.name: agent-diff-viewer
projects.hook: A browser-based diff viewer that shows AI agent code changes visually, with test impact and selective undo — so developers can trust, debug, and control agent output.
projects.situation: When an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) finishes a multi-file edit session...
projects.motivation: I want to see exactly what changed, what might break, and revert specific edits...
projects.outcome: So I can ship agent-generated code with confidence instead of anxiety.
projects.what_hurts: Terminal diffs are sequential noise — developers lose context across files, miss risky edits, and spend 5-15 minutes per incident tracing breakage back to specific agent changes.
projects.cost_today: 5-15 minutes per debug incident (daily for teams), missed regressions that reach production, eroding trust in AI tools.

functional: Show multi-file diffs in one visual view with syntax highlighting
Correlate test failures to specific file changes
Allow selective revert of individual edits without breaking deps
Flag files the agent touched outside the requested scope
Load in under 2 seconds from any git state
emotional: Feel confident approving agent changes
Feel in control, not at the mercy of the agent
Reduce the anxiety of 'what did it actually do?'
social: Demonstrate to the team that AI-generated code gets proper review
Build trust in AI tooling adoption across the org

forces.push: Terminal diffs are unreadable for multi-file agent changes. Developers miss things, ship regressions, lose trust in their AI tools.
forces.pull: Visual, instant, integrated diff view that shows what changed + what might break. Feels like GitHub PR review but for local agent sessions.
forces.habit: git diff, VS Code built-in diff, and GitHub PRs already work for 80% of cases. Developers have muscle memory for these tools.
forces.anxiety: Another tool in the stack. Will it be slow? Will it require context-switching? Will it break on large diffs or edge cases?

outputs: Browser-based visual diff viewer (HTML, local or served)
CLI command that opens the viewer from any git state
Optional Claude Code hook for auto-launch after edits
guardrails: Must load in under 2 seconds
No cloud dependency — works fully local
No login or account required
Must handle diffs of 50+ files without choking
CLI-first, browser is the viewer not the workflow

before_after.before: Scrolling terminal output, mentally compiling changes across files, asking the agent 'what did you change?', 10-minute debug sessions tracing test failures to specific edits.
before_after.after: One visual view, instantly see scope and risk, click to revert a single edit, test failures mapped to the change that caused them.

scenarios.title: Debug the breakage
scenarios.vignette: Tests fail after a Claude Code session. Dev opens the diff viewer, sees 6 files changed, clicks the failing test — it highlights the function edit that broke it. Reverts that one change. Tests pass. 90 seconds, not 10 minutes.

scenarios.title: Review before approve
scenarios.vignette: Claude Code says 'I've updated 8 files.' Dev opens the viewer, scans the file tree heat map, spots that the agent also touched .env. Flags it, approves the rest. Catches a mistake before it ships.

scenarios.title: Selective undo
scenarios.vignette: Agent refactored 5 utility functions. 4 are great, 1 introduced a subtle bug. Dev clicks that one function's diff, hits revert. The other 4 changes stay. No git surgery required.

scenarios.title: Question the reasoning
scenarios.vignette: Dev sees an unexpected import added. Clicks it, asks 'why?' inline. The tool shows the agent's reasoning from the session context. Dev decides to keep it.

quotes.text: When tests break, the tool pays for itself immediately. Job 1 is the prevention version of Job 4.
The real problem isn't seeing the scope — it's deciding 'is this safe?'
A diff viewer that shows 'hey, this file wasn't in your request' would be huge.
I want to click a change and ask Claude 'why did you do this?' without leaving the tool.
Show me which file edits are most likely to have caused test X to fail.
Not just what changed, but: anything built on my own time/machine outside of cohort sessions stays mine.

weaknesses: synthetic respondents, not real interviews
no actual usage data
open_questions: Should test impact analysis be built-in or pluggable?
How to access agent reasoning/session context for 'why?' feature?
Editor extension vs standalone tool vs Claude Code hook?
Free OSS or paid product?

projects.name: cull
projects.hook: A local-first image library for AI-heavy creative workflows that keeps provenance, ratings, and selection state in one place so teams can review faster and handoff confidently.
projects.situation: When I inherit or generate large image batches across generators, cameras, or folders and need to decide what to keep, share, and use next without losing context or waiting for manual file handoffs.
projects.motivation: I want one place to find the right image quickly, understand how it was created, and move review decisions through to export or handoff.
projects.outcome: So my team can review, approve, and reuse visual output faster while avoiding context loss and provenance mistakes.
projects.what_hurts: Image streams arrive in mixed directories with inconsistent names and missing decision history. Reviewers burn time hunting, re-opening files, and re-deriving context, then still need a separate path to share and approve remotely.

functional: Import and index local image sets without deleting source files
Attach generation metadata (provider, model, settings, seed) from sidecars when available
Support fast filtering by prompt, source, model, dates, ratings, tags, and visual similarity
Capture rating/selection and collection decisions as persistent, auditable local state
Surface provenance evidence so selection can be justified during review or delivery
Run remote review sessions through a streamable browser HTTP endpoint
Preserve workflow continuity across local/offline and connected review states
emotional: Feel confident that selections are recoverable and explainable after a long session
Feel in control of a large visual backlog instead of overwhelmed by it
Feel free to collaborate remotely without waiting for file copy cycles
social: Reduce friction for creative directors and clients in approval loops
Support teams that need shared decisions without local file transfer bottlenecks
Protect trust in production by making provenance auditable

forces.push: Thousands of images without a consistent context layer, mixed folder/import sources, and slow manual triage across previews, exports, and chat-based feedback.
forces.pull: A single application that connects local-first cataloging, generation metadata, and remote viewing so review and handoff become a contiguous loop.
forces.habit: Teams currently keep using manual folders, Preview windows, and ad-hoc sharing habits because they already exist and are familiar, even when they are slow.
forces.anxiety: Risk of exposing or losing data in a shared review path, and risk of losing local truth if a new layer adds complexity.

outputs: Local catalog and selection workspace in a Tauri desktop app
Queryable SQLite-backed image metadata and provenance store
Smart collections, rating model, and selection persistence
Streaming browser read path (shareable HTTP) for remote review
Export or handoff workflows that preserve selected outputs and rationale
guardrails: Preserve user-owned files: no implicit deletion or destructive file moves in core flows
Do not rely on network calls for core import, filter, and rating operations
Remote sharing must remain explicit and auditable so accidental exposure is visible
Keep local selections and provenance as source of truth even when remote review is active
target_users: AI artists iterating on high-volume generation
Creative directors managing client concept rounds
Small studios handling rights-aware delivery and review

before_after.before: Images land across folders or tools, review loops include hunting through files, and approvals happen through repeated export-and-share exchanges.
before_after.after: Images are indexed with evidence and decisions attached, reviews happen in a shared stream when needed, and selected outputs are carried forward with provenance intact.

scenarios.title: AI iteration history
scenarios.vignette: An artist generates dozens of variants per prompt and needs to recover the exact context for a later round. Cull keeps run metadata and selection state so the best candidates remain findable.

scenarios.title: Campaign concept review
scenarios.vignette: A creative director triages 200 concept images and tags high-fit options by project direction, style, and quality while preparing stakeholder approvals.

scenarios.title: Cross-tool prompt optimization
scenarios.vignette: A prompt engineer compares outputs from Midjourney, SD, DALL-E, and Gemini by model/source and visual similarity to decide what to keep or regenerate.

scenarios.title: Provenance-first handoff
scenarios.vignette: A studio lead must prove source evidence before handoff. Cull keeps sidecar and source signals alongside selections so origin questions can be answered quickly.

scenarios.title: Reusable reference library
scenarios.vignette: A creator starts a new project and needs to recall prior visual references quickly; Cull returns close matches and previously selected assets from an existing library.

scenarios.title: Remote review replacement for tethering
scenarios.vignette: An off-site editor needs to review fresh captures quickly; Cull exposes a public or tunnelled stream to the active library and they can approve/reject without local file transfer.

projects.name: humane-agentic-design
projects.actor: Gleb (author and first user) + three external actors: solo founders shipping products with agents; designers entering the agentic era (AI lab / AGENCY community members); and agents themselves, consulting the method autonomously before UX changes [Q3].
projects.context: meta-project: the set distributes other projects of this corpus (jtbd-skill, layout-rules)
projects.hook: Humane Agentic Design — a thematic plugin set (Impeccable-style dedicated repo): a human-centric design method cycle for people and agents, from JTBD to design system, installable into any agentic stack with one command.
projects.situation: When design skills pile up scattered across a personal folder and a shared repo — «it's just too noisy and hard to maintain» [Q1] — while founders and designers around are shipping interface slop with agents, without a method...
projects.motivation: I want to package the proven cycle (jtbd → persona → tokens/brand → layout-rules → nielsen-audit → before-after) into one installable, universally agentic plugin with a short namespace...
projects.outcome: So that every project of mine starts with the humane cycle, lab members install it with one command, the set earns its keep in client work, and people outside my circle install it too [Q4]. Numeric targets not set — unknown.
projects.what_hurts: Skills are scattered across ~/.claude/skills and the claude-skills repo with no versions and no namespace; duplicates drift apart; sharing the set means 'copy this folder'; Claude-specific bits (paths, tool names) block portability to Codex and other agents [Q1, Q2].

functional: One-command install: /plugin marketplace add, plus npx skills for non-Claude agents [Q2]
Short namespace humane:* — the plugin name is the invocation UX
A coherent cycle in the README, not a folder of skills: every skill knows its place in the method
Self-contained skills: no absolute paths, no Claude-only tools in the core
An entry in the agency-plugins marketplace (option 2 — aggregator on top of the dedicated repo)
emotional: Order instead of noise: one place, one version, nothing drifts [Q1]
social: A showcase of the method: the LinkedIn audience and lab members see a coherent product, not a scatter [Q4]

forces.push: The noise and unmaintainability of the scatter: «it's just too noisy and hard to maintain» [Q1]; the ~/.claude/skills vs repo duplicates have already drifted once.
forces.pull: The Impeccable pattern: one repo = plugin + its own marketplace, a cycle narrative, a namespace, versions; universal agent support widens the audience from 'my Claude skills' to a method for any agent [Q2].
forces.habit: partial — the personal skills folder works fine for a single user; the inertia is small but real: familiar short names without a prefix, and instant in-place edits without a commit.
forces.anxiety: partial [creator-derived, not interviewed]: one more repo to maintain; risk of breaking working skills during the move (jtbd carries scripts/templates); cross-agent compatibility may drift; the dual channel (plugin + npx skills) means double testing.

outputs: Repo glebis/humane-agentic-design: the humane plugin + its own marketplace.json
Core (7): jtbd, layout-rules, design-tokens, persona-review, synthetic-respondent (agent), nielsen-heuristics, before-after

README cycle narrative + an agency-plugins entry (git-subdir)

projects.situation: When I'm iterating on AI-generated image series across multiple tools (ChatGPT, MidJourney, DALL-E) and the outputs land in scattered folders with dozens of Preview windows piling up...

projects.hook: A real-time knowledge capture platform that turns 2-hour technical sessions into structured, interactive, AI-queryable libraries — replacing slides, manual summaries, and scattered notes.
projects.situation: When I run a 2-hour technical session for 10+ community members, covering more material than we can explore live...
projects.motivation: I want to automatically capture, structure, and publish everything discussed — ideas, tools, terms, links, prompts, exercises — as interconnected knowledge nodes...
projects.outcome: So participants get a browsable knowledge base (not a recording link), can try prompts and produce artifacts during the session, and future members can catch up without watching a 2-hour video.
projects.what_hurts: Knowledge dies with the session. A recording exists but nobody scrubs through 120 minutes to find the one tool name mentioned at minute 47. After the session, I manually write summaries (1+ hour), losing participants' perspective on what mattered to them. Presentations are static — participants consume but don't produce.
projects.cost_today: 1+ hour per session writing summaries. Participants forget 80% within a week. New members have no structured way to catch up. Knowledge lives in 5 disconnected systems (Obsidian, agency-docs, Granola, HTML slides, Live Companion).

Produce shareable artifacts (PDF, video, formatted docs) during the session from embedded prompts
Full analysis of entire transcript with deduplication
Search and filter across all sessions and all node types
AI-queryable: agents can pull 'all tools from Session 3' or 'homework for week 2'

Participants leave with artifacts they made, not slides they watched.

forces.anxiety: Will participants actually engage or will it distract from the session? Will AI extract garbage that embarrasses me? Will tech break live (it did — 429 errors, analysis stopping, blank screens)? Is this overengineering for a 10-person community?

projects.name: pos-interactive-mode
projects.hook: A full-screen TUI for pos so a power user can browse focuses, projects and live sessions, act on them with one keypress, and reach any of the 24 commands without recalling its name or arguments.
projects.situation: When I'm in my cmux cockpit and want to switch focus, open a project, load a preset, or run a less-frequent pos command but can't remember the exact command name or argument order...
projects.motivation: I want to browse what exists and pick from a live list with arrow keys, then act with a single keypress...
projects.outcome: So I can drive the whole cockpit without breaking flow to run `pos help` and re-type names I just read on screen.
projects.what_hurts: pos is 24 flag-driven commands. To act on a focus/project/session I read its name from command output, then re-type it as an argument. For infrequent commands I stop and run `pos help` first. Multi-step intents (create a project = edit focus.toml + new workspace + load) have no single entry point.
projects.cost_today: Context-switch tax on every navigation: recall + re-type, or a help detour. The richest part of pos (live workspaces, git status per project) is locked behind commands you must already know.

functional: Browse focuses, projects, and live sessions in navigable panes
Show live git status (dirty markers) inline while browsing
Act on a selection with a single keypress: open, load, cc, new
Reach every one of the 24 commands via a command palette (escalation path)
Confirm before any destructive action (rm, load which closes tabs)
emotional: In control of the cockpit without memorizing it
Confident no stray keypress closes a tab or kills a session

forces.push: Re-typing names just read from output; forgetting which of 24 commands exist; a `pos help` detour mid-flow; multi-step flows with no single entry point.
forces.pull: Arrow-select from a live list with inline git status, single-keypress actions, and a searchable palette for the long tail — browse instead of memorize.
forces.habit: Muscle memory of `pos <cmd> <name>`; the `pos help` → read → re-type loop for anything not memorized.
forces.anxiety: An interactive layer could fire a destructive action (close tabs via load/rm) on a mistaken keypress, or break the agent-first JSON contract that other tooling depends on.

outputs: A full-screen curses TUI launched by pos with no/one subcommand on a TTY
Navigation-first layout (focuses -> projects/sessions -> actions) escalating to a command palette
Each action dispatches the existing pos command path unchanged
guardrails: Never run a destructive action (rm, load) without explicit confirmation
Engage only on a real TTY; never when piped or invoked by an agent (preserve JSON contract)
No heavy TUI framework dependency; stdlib curses or already-present tools only
Additive: every existing `pos <cmd>` keeps working exactly as today
weaknesses: Actor is the tool's author/sole user (n-of-1); no external validation
No verbatim quote captured; trigger answers are self-reported multi-select, not a narrated incident

outcomes.statement: Minimize recall needed to reach an infrequent command

projects.name: sound-out
projects.hook: An optional voice layer for cenno's ask_user prompts on the Mac: the agent speaks its question aloud and you answer by voice, so you can step away from the screen and stay in the loop with your agent hands-free.
projects.situation: When I'm away from the keyboard during an agent session — in the kitchen, headphones on listening to music — and the agent pops a cenno question that's blocking its work...
projects.motivation: I want to hear the question, judge whether it's worth answering now or fine to skip, and answer by voice without walking back to stare at the screen...
projects.outcome: So I can keep an agent moving while I'm doing something else, and only get pulled in for things that actually matter.
projects.what_hurts: cenno prompts are screen-and-keyboard bound: if I'm not staring at the popup I miss it or it stalls the agent, and even when I see it I have to type/click. I'm tethered to the desk for what should be a quick yes/no. There's also no signal of urgency — a trivial question interrupts the same as a blocking one.
projects.cost_today: Lost agent throughput while it waits on me, and the friction of being chained to the screen during long sessions.

functional: Read the cenno prompt aloud (TTS) as an opt-in per-prompt or per-session toggle, reusing the existing dictation window

Process the structured/markdown prompt into speakable text: flatten **bold**, strip markdown, and voice code-ish identifiers (file paths, branch names like refactor/i5ly.4-split-db-rs, db.rs) sensibly rather than reading raw syntax
Capture the spoken answer via STT (Whisper) — the dictation window already does this
Pluggable TTS providers via config — Groq, OpenAI, Cartesia, ElevenLabs — switchable without code changes; the agent may configure it
Support emotional/prosody markup for providers that accept it; degrade gracefully for those that don't
Support ElevenLabs sound/music generation API: generate arbitrary sounds (earcons, alert tones, ambient) from a text prompt, usable as urgency cues
Convey priority hands-free — only sound out / interrupt for high-priority or blocking questions; stay quiet for minor ones

Priority model: 3 levels P0/P1/P2 set per prompt (defaults to P1 when the agent doesn't specify — never silently P0). P0 is always shown and sounded regardless of settings. A user-adjustable threshold (in project config) sets the level at/above which prompts are read aloud; P1/P2 are gated by it plus voice-mode being on.
emotional: Feel untethered — able to walk away and trust the agent will reach me when it matters
Feel like a real back-and-forth with the agent, not filling out a form
Feel in control of when audio is and isn't appropriate (easy to silence in public)

forces.push: Being chained to the screen to answer prompts; missing or delaying the agent when I step away (kitchen, headphones); every question interrupts equally regardless of importance.
forces.pull: Hands-free hear-and-answer while away or with headphones on; a more conversational, modern feel; the agent reaching me by sound only when it's worth it.
forces.habit: The existing dictation window already works 'okay-ish'; reading the popup and typing/clicking is the entrenched path; staring at the screen during sessions.
forces.anxiety: TTS mispronouncing critical details or losing information so I can't tell what's going on; contexts where audio is wrong (coffee shop, don't want headphones in public); privacy of spoken prompts/answers.

outputs: Spoken rendering of cenno prompts
Voice-captured answers fed back to the agent
Optionally generated audio cues (earcons/alert tones) per priority via ElevenLabs
guardrails: Opt-in, not default-on — must be trivially silenceable for public/quiet contexts
Never lose or distort the substance of a prompt when converting to speech
v1 is one-shot (speak question, capture one answer), NOT multi-turn dialog
v1 is Mac cenno only — iOS companion is a later want, not v1 scope

trigger.detail: Fires when cenno surfaces an ask_user prompt and voice-out is enabled (gated by priority)

quotes.text: I was maybe away from the computer and at kitchen and I would have heard and would come faster. And I would have known whether it's a question I need to answer quickly or that it's okay to skip it.
I don't want to be staring at the screen all the time... I'm wearing my headphones, I'm listening to some music, then I get this message from my agent, and yes, I wanna know what's going on.

If it's really urgent, if it's blocking something that I have evaluated as high priority... we might need some kind of priorities for all the tasks. I don't wanna be interrupted with questions that are really minor.
On the Mac only. Let's start with one shot. Technically we already have this window where you can use dictation, so maybe it's okay to reuse it. So we just add an optional voice out.
Maybe if it pronounces incorrectly some critical stuff or some details are lost for some reason, I cannot understand what is going on.

open_questions: Text-processing rules: exact normalization for markdown + code identifiers (file paths, branch names, dotted filenames) — a real example prompt was provided (db-refactor commit question) to derive rules from
Where TTS/STT/provider config and the sound-out threshold live in project config, and how the agent is allowed to set a per-prompt priority + configure providers
Whether generated ElevenLabs earcons map 1:1 to priority levels, and whether they're pre-generated/cached or generated on demand
Public-context handling: manual mute vs. context/quiet-hours awareness

projects.name: vers1-io
projects.hook: Рабочее пространство для согласования видео: монтажёр заливает черновой монтаж, заказчик оставляет правки прямо по таймкоду (текстом, голосом, пометкой на кадре) по ссылке без регистрации — вместо голосовых «на 2:34 поправь цвет» в Telegram.
projects.situation: Когда я монтажёр или продюсер в студии и веду проект с 3-4 итерациями правок, а файлы и комментарии заказчика расползлись по Telegram-чату и Яндекс.Диску...
projects.motivation: ...я хочу собрать все правки, версии и статусы в одном месте с привязкой к конкретному кадру...
projects.outcome: ...чтобы не тратить время на пересборку контекста («какую правку я уже сделал?», «это про вторую или третью версию?») и не находить потерянную правку на этапе сдачи, когда переделывать дороже.
projects.what_hurts: Правки живут в чате и теряются в скролле. Таймкод — на словах, «плюс-минус секунда». Голосовое на 40 секунд нужно переслушать, чтобы найти суть. Версии — это файлы вида final_v3_new_2.mp4. Нет статуса «сделано / не сделано» по каждой правке. Telegram пережимает видео, из-за чего по нему нельзя оценивать цвет.
projects.cost_today: Заявлено на сайте: 20-30 минут в день на проекте с 3-4 итерациями уходит на «найти и вспомнить». ВНИМАНИЕ: цифра вендорская, источник не указан, замеров нет.

social: Выглядеть студией с процессом, а не переписки в чате
Снимать вопросы юридического отдела заказчика российской юрисдикцией и офертой на русском

forces.push: Через день-два в чате пять версий файла, три голосовых по 40 секунд и переписка «а это про какую версию было?». Правка всплывает на сдаче, когда переделывать дороже. Для тех, кто был на Frame.io: Adobe не принимает карты РФ и не выставляет счета юрлицам — платить приходится через посредников с риском блокировки аккаунта.
forces.pull: Клик по таймлайну вместо переслушивания голосового. Голос сам превращается в текст. Версии — вкладки одного файла. У каждой правки статус. Рублёвый тариф с Free-входом без карты. Данные в РФ — снимает вопрос 152-ФЗ у безопасников заказчика.
forces.habit: Telegram + Яндекс.Диск: быстро, привычно, нулевой порог входа, заказчику ничего не надо осваивать. Сайт сам признаёт: если правок мало и участников двое — Telegram отлично справляется.
forces.anxiety: Что придётся перестраивать пайплайн: C2C-плагин Frame.io для Premiere Pro не переносится, автоматизации под API Frame.io надо переписывать. Плюс невысказанный на сайте страх: согласится ли заказчик уйти из привычного чата.

before_after.before: Видно: чат с пятью mp4 и голосовыми, отдельный документ со списком правок. Ощущается: постоянный страх, что что-то потеряно.
before_after.after: Видно: один таймлайн, под ним лента правок со статусами, вкладки версий. Ощущается: список закрывается сам, ничего не надо держать в голове.

weaknesses: evidence_quote = 0: на сайте НЕТ ни одной цитаты клиента, отзыва, кейса, логотипа или имени студии. Фразы «на 2:34 поправь цвет», «примерно тут», final_v3_new_2.mp4 написаны маркетингом вендора как иллюстрация, а не собраны у пользователей.
measurable_outcome = 1: единственная цифра боли (20-30 мин/день) — вендорская оценка без методики и источника.
actor_specificity = 1: роли названы (монтажёр, фрилансер, студия, агентство, продакшен), но нет ни одного конкретного описанного актора с контекстом.
ГЕЙТ НЕ ПРОЙДЕН. Это гипотеза JTBD, реконструированная из маркетинговых материалов, а не валидированный JTBD. Все switch forces — то, что вендор ДУМАЕТ про своего пользователя.
open_questions: Кто уже платит? На сайте ноль отзывов, кейсов, логотипов и цифр вроде «N студий». Непонятно, есть ли traction вообще.
Откуда 20-30 минут в день? Замеряли на реальных командах или оценили? Без методики цифра не работает в продаже корпоративному клиенту.
Кто инициатор перехода — монтажёр или заказчик? Habit-сила живёт на стороне заказчика, а платит студия. Сайт нигде не отвечает, что делать, если клиент отказывается уходить из Telegram.

Free-тариф ставит водяной знак vers1.io на ВСЕ видео. Покажет ли студия заказчику черновик с чужим вотермарком? Если нет — Free не демонстрирует ценность на реальном проекте, а именно это обещает CTA.
Технические лимиты нигде не указаны: максимальный размер файла, поддерживаемые кодеки и контейнеры, ProRes, 4K, скорость загрузки. Для продакшена это вопрос номер один.
«Экспорт в основные монтажные программы» — в какие именно и как? Premiere, DaVinci, Final Cut? Через XML/EDL? Прямой замены C2C нет, но чем заменяют — не сказано.
Лимиты AI: на Team «умные функции без ограничений», значит на Pro ограничения есть — какие? Точность расшифровки русской речи не заявлена.
AI на YandexGPT упомянут только на сравнительной странице с Frame.io, на главной — просто «ИИ». Для 152-ФЗ-чувствительного клиента это важная деталь, спрятанная не там.

Заявления о безопасности на /trust (TLS 1.3, AES-128 HLS, форензик-маркировка, SSO/SAML) ничем не подтверждены: нет аттестации, сертификатов, аудита, пентеста. Для Business-тарифа от 14 990 ₽ это будет первым вопросом безопасника.

Страницы /trust и /developers не видны в верхней навигации (только в подвале) и не отдаются в HTML — рендерятся на клиенте. Ровно те материалы, которые продают дорогие тарифы, хуже всего доступны и не индексируются.
Documentation для разработчиков — на английском, весь остальной сайт — на русском. Для кого она: для российских интеграторов или это задел под экспорт?
Что удерживает после проекта? Тарификация от объёма хранилища создаёт давление «удали старое», а сценария архива/ретеншена нет. Не описано, что происходит с проектами и ссылками при отмене подписки.
Нет мобильного сценария. Заказчик часто смотрит черновик с телефона — работает ли комментирование по таймкоду на мобильном, не сказано.
Сегмент не выбран: Free/Pro (фрилансер) и Business (продакшен с госзаказчиком и форензик-маркировкой) — это две разные компании с разной продажей. Кто целевой — из сайта не следует.
Нет ответа, что происходит при отмене санкционных ограничений или возврате Frame.io: половина позиционирования держится на «нельзя заплатить из РФ», это заимствованное преимущество, а не собственное.
